title: Kellogg to Remove Artificial Colors from Its Cereals
paragraphs: The cereal maker Kellogg has announced that it will remove all artificial colors from its cereals in the United States by the end of 2026, a full year earlier than it had originally planned.

The company made the announcement in August. Popular cereals such as Froot Loops and Apple Jacks, which are known for their bright colors, will now use colors made from natural sources, including fruit and vegetable juices. According to one report, turmeric will be used for yellow, and annatto, a seed from a tropical tree, will be used for orange. The new products are expected to arrive in stores across the country before the end of December.
In addition, Kellogg is removing BHT, an artificial preservative, from the small number of cereals that still contain it.
Doug VanDeVelde, the company's chief growth officer, said that more and more consumers are looking for foods made with simple, recognizable ingredients.

The company has faced pressure to make these changes for some time. In 2024, protesters delivered petitions with 400,000 signatures to Kellogg's headquarters, asking it to remove artificial dyes and BHT. Kellogg had already removed these ingredients from its cereals in other countries, including Canada.

The US government has also been pushing for change. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has urged food companies to stop using artificial dyes made from petroleum. In 2025, Kellogg agreed with the state of Texas to remove these dyes from its cereals by the end of 2027.

Retailers are also playing a role. The store chain Target said it would stop selling cereals with artificial colors by the end of May, and Walmart said it will remove artificial colors from its own store brands by January 2027. Other large food companies, such as Kraft and General Mills, have also promised to remove artificial dyes from their products in the US by 2027.
